statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Cannot determine from the provided facts whether 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 targets conduct done “for the purpose of evading” Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements (e.g., causing or attempting to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report, or structuring/assisting in structuring transactions to evade such reporting). The fact pattern shows multiple transactions (including several cash transactions, some above $10,000) by a cash-intensive convenience/grocery business, but it does not specify (i) whether any transactions were structured into multiple sub-$10,000 cash deposits/withdrawals on the same day or in a manner designed to avoid a Currency Transaction Report threshold, (ii) whether the entity or any person acted with the purpose of evading reporting, or (iii) whether any required report was avoided or a bank was caused/attempted to be caused not to file. Because the key mens rea/purpose element and any evasion pattern are not established, the statute’s elements cannot be confirmed on these facts. Contiguous phrase in answer: “31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring”.
